Use continuous direct assessment of ventilation/airway as well as ECG, pulse oximetry, continuous capnography and NIBP whenever feasible; prepare oxygen, suction, bag-mask ventilation, airway adjuncts, vasopressor and reversal agents before dosing.
- The following adult reference regimens are from RCEM 2022; ACEP 2026 does not prescribe these doses: ketamine 1 mg/kg IV over 30--60 seconds, repeat 0.25--0.5 mg/kg every 5--10 minutes; propofol 0.5--1 mg/kg IV slowly, repeat 0.5 mg/kg every 3--5 minutes; midazolam 1--2 mg IV over 1--2 minutes with small repeat doses after 2--5 minutes; fentanyl 0.5 mcg/kg IV with another sedative or 0.5--1 mcg/kg when used for analgesia/sedation, repeat no sooner than every 2 minutes. Reduce substantially in older, frail, shocked or opioid-exposed patients.
- Match agent to physiology and procedure: ketamine provides analgesia/dissociation but may increase secretions or sympathetic demand; propofol is not analgesic and can cause apnea/hypotension; midazolam plus opioid has synergistic respiratory depression and delayed effect; local/regional anesthesia reduces sedative requirement.
- Prepare naloxone and flumazenil but prioritize airway/ventilation. Titrate naloxone in 0.1--0.2 mg IV increments to ventilation; flumazenil 0.1--0.2 mg IV every minute to a maximum 1 mg is conditional and may precipitate seizure/withdrawal.
- Continuous ICU analgesia/sedation in intubated patients is covered by `icu-sedation-analgesia-infusions`; this module is procedural sedation only.
- Record intended and achieved depth, drug/time/dose, capnography and adverse events. Continue observation until baseline mental status, stable vitals, airway independence, pain/nausea control and safe discharge/admission criteria are met. Discharge to a responsible adult with verbal/written instructions; admission/transfer requires a structured handover.

title: Icu Sedation Analgesia Infusions
sharedPreamble:
# Procedure and pharmacology modules

Shared gate: verify identity, indication, consent/capacity, monitoring, allergies,
weight, pregnancy, renal/hepatic function, anticoagulation, equipment, skilled help,
rescue plan and post-intervention reassessment.

- For oral liquid/drop formulations, always retain the dose in mg and calculate mL only from the exact verified concentration. If the exact marketed product is dispensed as drops, also display whole drops per dose only from a verified mg/drop or drops/mL factor; never assume a universal drop factor.
sectionBody:
- Scope: adult, intubated/ICU continuous analgesia and sedation (draft v1.35, human review pending). Procedural sedation remains in `sedoanalgesia`; RSI induction in `airway-rsi`; pediatric infusions are out of scope. Always apply `medication-selection-safety`.
- Analgesia first: assess pain before sedating, using self-report (0--10 NRS) when possible and CPOT or BPS when the patient cannot self-report (PADIS 2018). Use an assessment-driven, protocol-based stepwise approach and multimodal opioid-sparing adjuncts (PADIS 2018, conditional).
- Sedation depth: set and document a target at least daily. PADIS 2018 suggests light rather than deep sedation (conditional, low quality; light is about RASS -2 to +1). Either daily sedative interruption or nurse-protocolized targeted sedation can achieve light sedation (ungraded). Coordinate awakening with spontaneous breathing trials when safety screens are met. Deep sedation is reserved for specific indications (e.g. refractory hypoxemia with ventilator dyssynchrony, neuromuscular blockade, raised ICP, status epilepticus) and must be explicitly justified and reassessed.
- Sedative choice: PADIS 2018 suggests propofol or dexmedetomidine over benzodiazepines (conditional, low quality). The PADIS 2025 focused update suggests dexmedetomidine over propofol when light sedation and/or delirium reduction are highest priorities (conditional, moderate certainty), but not for patients needing deep sedation or at high bradycardia risk. It found insufficient evidence to recommend benzodiazepines for anxiety. Screen for delirium (e.g. CAM-ICU) every shift.
- Arithmetic rules: state total drug, diluent, final volume and concentration; show `mL/h = dose (micrograms/kg/min) x kg x 60 / concentration (micrograms/mL)`, or for per-hour doses `mL/h = (dose per kg per hour x kg) / concentration`. Worked 70 kg examples are arithmetic references only; local standard concentrations override. Before a bolus, check BP; in shock reduce or avoid boluses and titrate slowly. Before stopping infusions of several days, taper to limit withdrawal.
- **Fentanyl** (preferred opioid for hemodynamic instability/renal impairment in many ICUs): infusion range 0.7--10 micrograms/kg/h (KSCCM 2021 PADIS table; start low after titrated boluses to CPOT/BPS). The UK SmPC infusion of about 0.1 micrograms/kg/min is written for operative anaesthesia and is not an ICU starting dose. Preparation: **1,000 micrograms (20 mL of 50 micrograms/mL) to a final volume of 100 mL = 10 micrograms/mL** in glucose 5% or sodium chloride 0.9% (SmPC). 70 kg at 0.7 micrograms/kg/h: 0.7 x 70 = 49 micrograms/h; 49 / 10 = 4.9 mL/h; at 1.5 micrograms/kg/h = 105 micrograms/h = 10.5 mL/h. Lipophilic accumulation with prolonged infusion; CYP3A4 inhibitors increase exposure; serotonergic co-medication risk.
- **Remifentanil**: UK SmPC ICU start 0.1--0.15 micrograms/kg/min, adjust by 0.025 micrograms/kg/min at intervals of at least 5 minutes; if analgesia is inadequate at 0.2 micrograms/kg/min add a sedative; SmPC range 0.006--0.74 micrograms/kg/min; boluses not recommended in ICU; studied up to 3 days. Before stopping, establish alternative analgesia and reduce by 25% decrements at least 10 minutes apart (rapid offset causes abrupt pain). Preparation: **5 mg to a final volume of 100 mL = 50 micrograms/mL** (SmPC range 20--50 micrograms/mL). 70 kg at 0.1 micrograms/kg/min: 0.1 x 70 x 60 = 420 micrograms/h; 420 / 50 = 8.4 mL/h; each 0.025 step = 2.1 mL/h.
- **Morphine and hydromorphone**: less suitable for continuous ICU infusion when renal/hepatic function is impaired or unstable because active metabolites/parent drug accumulate (KSCCM 2021 notes accumulation in organ dysfunction); morphine also releases histamine. Reference ranges (KSCCM 2021): morphine 2--30 mg/h, hydromorphone 0.5--3 mg/h; not weight-based. Preparation: morphine **100 mg to 100 mL = 1 mg/mL**: 2 mg/h = 2 mL/h. Hydromorphone **10 mg to 100 mL = 0.1 mg/mL**: 0.5 mg/h = 5 mL/h. Verify the product strength (high-potency hydromorphone presentations exist) and local restrictions before use.
- **Propofol**: US label ICU sedation start 5 micrograms/kg/min (0.3 mg/kg/h), increase by 5--10 micrograms/kg/min with at least 5 minutes between adjustments; most patients need 5--50 micrograms/kg/min (0.3--3 mg/kg/h); do not exceed 4 mg/kg/h without careful risk-benefit review. Preparation: **undiluted 10 mg/mL (1%; 1,000 mg in a 100 mL vial)**; 20 mg/mL presentations halve the mL/h. 70 kg at 5 micrograms/kg/min: 5 x 70 x 60 = 21,000 micrograms/h = 21 mg/h; 21 / 10 = 2.1 mL/h; at 25 micrograms/kg/min = 10.5 mL/h; at 50 micrograms/kg/min = 21 mL/h; 4 mg/kg/h = 280 mg/h = 28 mL/h. Not analgesic; causes hypotension and respiratory depression. Lipid 0.1 g/mL, about 1.1 kcal/mL: include in nutrition. Check triglycerides at baseline/early and periodically during prolonged or high-dose use (no universal threshold verified in this review). **PRIS**: suspect with unexplained metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia, rhabdomyolysis/rising CK, arrhythmia, AKI or rising triglycerides, especially with high doses (label highlights more than 5 mg/kg/h for more than 48 hours) or concurrent catecholamines/steroids; stop propofol and switch sedative. Strict asepsis; discard tubing and product per label interval (12 hours).
- **Dexmedetomidine**: EU SmPC (Dexdor) start 0.7 micrograms/kg/h, adjust stepwise within 0.2--1.4 micrograms/kg/h (do not exceed 1.4); a loading dose is not recommended (more adverse reactions); a new level may take up to 1 hour. Intended for sedation no deeper than RASS 0 to -3; not suitable alone when deep sedation is required. Preparation: **400 micrograms (4 mL of 100 micrograms/mL) to a final volume of 100 mL = 4 micrograms/mL** (SmPC allows 4 or 8 micrograms/mL). 70 kg at 0.7 micrograms/kg/h: 0.7 x 70 = 49 micrograms/h; 49 / 4 = 12.25 mL/h; 0.2 micrograms/kg/h = 3.5 mL/h; 1.4 micrograms/kg/h = 24.5 mL/h. Bradycardia (about 25%) and hypotension (about 13%) are common; contraindicated with second/third-degree AV block without pacing, uncontrolled hypotension and acute cerebrovascular conditions. The SmPC warns of increased mortality with dexmedetomidine in patients aged 65 years or younger versus alternative sedatives (SPICE III signal); weigh this in younger patients. Reduce in hepatic impairment; experience beyond 14 days is limited.
- **Midazolam**: third-line for continuous sedation; reserve for specific indications (e.g. seizures, alcohol withdrawal, need for deep sedation when propofol is unsuitable) because benzodiazepine infusions are associated with accumulation, prolonged ventilation and delirium. UK SmPC: maintenance 0.03--0.2 mg/kg/h; loading 0.03--0.3 mg/kg in small increments only if hemodynamically appropriate (reduce/omit in hypovolemia, vasoconstriction, hypothermia, older or debilitated patients). Preparation: **100 mg to a final volume of 100 mL = 1 mg/mL** in sodium chloride 0.9% or glucose 5% (confirm local standard; SmPC lists compatible diluents). 70 kg at 0.03 mg/kg/h: 0.03 x 70 = 2.1 mg/h = 2.1 mL/h; 0.1 mg/kg/h = 7 mL/h; 0.2 mg/kg/h = 14 mL/h. Accumulates with renal impairment (active glucuronide), hepatic dysfunction, obesity and CYP3A4 inhibitors; taper to avoid withdrawal.
- **Ketamine infusion (adjunct)**: PADIS 2018 suggests low-dose ketamine as an opioid-sparing adjunct in post-surgical ICU adults (conditional, very low quality): 0.5 mg/kg IV once, then 1--2 micrograms/kg/min. It is not a stand-alone long-term sedative in this module; the SmPC warns it is not for long-term use (cystitis, hepatotoxicity reported with prolonged use). Preparation: **100 mg to a final volume of 100 mL = 1 mg/mL** in glucose 5% or sodium chloride 0.9% (SmPC). 70 kg at 1 microgram/kg/min: 1 x 70 x 60 = 4,200 micrograms/h = 4.2 mg/h = 4.2 mL/h; 2 micrograms/kg/min = 8.4 mL/h; bolus 0.5 mg/kg = 35 mg. Watch hypertension/tachycardia, emergence phenomena and secretions.
- Hold/stop and reassess: over-sedation below the RASS target, hypotension needing vasopressor escalation attributable to sedation, bradycardia/AV block (dexmedetomidine), PRIS features (propofol), new delirium (review benzodiazepines/anticholinergics, sleep, mobility; PADIS 2025 suggests enhanced mobilization and melatonin, and makes no recommendation for or against antipsychotics for delirium treatment). Document target, achieved RASS and CPOT/BPS every nursing assessment.
- **Preparation review 14 November 2026 — YELLOW:** the guideline position and worked pump arithmetic have been reviewed; these do not validate every displayed mixture. Before a bedside pump table, record the exact product/strength and base-versus-salt expression, permitted diluent, final volume/concentration, container/tubing, route and co-infusion compatibility. Record physicochemical stability separately from microbiological in-use/hang time and the actual temperature/light conditions; use the shortest applicable limit. Do not extrapolate a foreign label or one product's time limit to another. Product-level reconciliation remains incomplete; no local pharmacy approval, stock or ready-to-use preparation is certified by this review. Propofol lipid-emulsion handling and each opioid/sedative preparation require their own product conditions; a common 24-hour replacement rule is not established.
- **Product sheets10--17 follow-up (14 November2026):** generic24--48h opioid/ketamine claims and broad Y-site lists supplied in the drafts are not blanket product approvals. Ketolar specifies immediate use after dilution. Normon midazolam dilution stability examples must not be extrapolated to1/2/5mg/mL without support. Dexdor allows4 or8micrograms/mL; product-specific microbiological conditions remain distinct. For Lipuro the diluted1%6h limit must not automatically be assigned to every undiluted syringe transfer, and neither4mg/kg/h nor7days guarantees absence of PRIS. Morphine is not routine acute-heart-failure treatment; palliation/analgesia are separate indications. The Edunix capsule link is not an injectable hydromorphone source or proof of national market absence. Exact sources,pending conditions and owner-reported reviewers are in `qa/INFUSION_PRODUCT_RECONCILIATION_2026-11-14.json`; no universal deep-sedation target or new high-dose rescue indication is introduced.
- **Uploaded PNT concentration change:** the draft proposes fentanyl50micrograms/mL rather than the earlier10micrograms/mL example, propofol2% (20mg/mL) rather than10mg/mL, and hydromorphone0.2mg/mL rather than0.1mg/mL. At the same dose their pump rates are respectively one-fifth, one-half and one-half of those examples. Recalculate from the verified product/recipe; this dimensional comparison is not approval of the prepared syringe or its hang time. The PNT supplies ketamine and other missing recipes but does not establish universal24h use or Y-site compatibility.
- **Owner-accepted replacement and Lipuro handling (14 November 2026):** start non-propofol preparations immediately after opening/reconstitution/dilution and replace the container/tubing by 24 h as a local upper limit, earlier when a shorter applicable limit or completion requires it; this does not authorize storage or prove chemical stability for every mixture, including Ketolar. For **Propofol Lipuro 1% diluted**, use within **6 h from dilution**, prepared aseptically immediately before administration; maximum dilution is **1 part propofol + 4 parts compatible diluent**, at least **2 mg/mL**. For **Lipuro 1% or 2% undiluted**, use an aseptically and immediately filled sterile syringe or original vial with immediate administration; replace the reservoir and complete line within **12 h from first opening/puncture**. A syringe transfer does not reset the clock or itself impose a manufacturer 6 h limit. Do not prefill/store an ordinary syringe for deferred use; it does not automatically acquire a 6/12 h storage allowance. Lipuro 2% must not be diluted. These product-specific limits supersede the local24h rule; no rule for a different commercial prefilled product is inferred.
- **Focused closure review14/11/2026:** all17 submitted sheets, the later PNT and owner decisions were considered. Clinical/pharmacy names and prior acceptance are retained without being requested again. Exact source-applicable concentration/material/in-use conditions are still needed for the candidate preparations listed in `qa/INFUSION_PRODUCT_RECONCILIATION_2026-11-14.json`; immediate start and a local24h replacement ceiling do not supply missing physicochemical stability. Therefore YELLOW and the existing blocked contracts remain; neither a foreign reference nor this review automatically enables a pump order.

title: Empiric Antibiotics
sharedPreamble:
# Procedure and pharmacology modules

Shared gate: verify identity, indication, consent/capacity, monitoring, allergies,
weight, pregnancy, renal/hepatic function, anticoagulation, equipment, skilled help,
rescue plan and post-intervention reassessment.

- For oral liquid/drop formulations, always retain the dose in mg and calculate mL only from the exact verified concentration. If the exact marketed product is dispensed as drops, also display whole drops per dose only from a verified mg/drop or drops/mL factor; never assume a universal drop factor.
sectionBody:
- Scope: framework for adult emergency empirical antimicrobial selection. It is **not** a universal regimen table. Agent choice must follow syndrome/source, severity, local resistance ecology, prior microbiology, allergy history, organ function, immune status, recent antibiotics, device exposure and local formulary.
- **Timing in sepsis (SSC 2026):** probable/definite sepsis without shock -> administer antimicrobials immediately, ideally **within 1 hour** of recognition. Possible sepsis without shock -> perform a rapid time-limited evaluation and, if concern for infection persists, give antimicrobials **within 3 hours** of first suspicion. Septic shock -> do not delay effective therapy for nonessential diagnostics.
- Obtain blood/other cultures before antibiotics when this can be done rapidly **without delaying** treatment in shock or another time-critical infection.
- **MDR coverage:** use empirical coverage for a specific MDR pathogen only when patient-level or local epidemiologic risk is high (e.g. previous colonization/infection, prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics, prolonged hospitalization/high-prevalence unit). If MDR risk is low, avoid reflex broad-spectrum MDR coverage. De-escalate promptly when microbiology and clinical response permit.
- **Anaerobes/antifungals:** do not add routine anaerobic coverage in sepsis without a plausible anaerobic source. Do not use routine empirical antifungal therapy in sepsis/septic shock; consider it only in selected patients with specific fungal-risk factors.
- **Source control:** identify an anatomic source requiring drainage/debridement/device removal and pursue early source control; SSC 2026 suggests ideally within **6 hours** once such a source is diagnosed in sepsis/septic shock.
- **Complicated UTI (IDSA 2025):** in sepsis attributed to cUTI/pyelonephritis, choose empirically among a **third- or fourth-generation cephalosporin, carbapenem, piperacillin-tazobactam, or fluoroquinolone** using a four-step assessment: severity, resistance risk, patient-specific factors, and—if septic—a current local antibiogram. If using an antibiogram, IDSA suggests aiming for approximately **>=90% susceptibility in septic shock** or **>=80% in sepsis without shock** for the relevant pathogens. Broader anti-Pseudomonas/MRSA/Enterococcus coverage is reserved for corresponding risk.
- **Do not infer local doses from this module.** Exact loading dose, maintenance dose, prolonged/extended infusion strategy, renal/hepatic adjustment, allergy alternative and compatibility must come from the syndrome-specific guideline plus current local hospital/Portugal-Azores formulary.
- Review at 24--48 h (or earlier when cultures return): confirm infection, narrow/stop unnecessary agents, optimize route/dose, document duration and source-control status. Procalcitonin should not replace clinical assessment when deciding whether to start therapy.
- **Empirical versus targeted therapy:** do not wait for the current patient's culture/susceptibility result to start time-critical empirical treatment. That result guides subsequent targeted adjustment; prior cultures and relevant local resistance data, when available, can already change the initial empirical choice. Lack of an uploaded local antibiogram does not block this general decision framework or justify delaying urgent antibiotics.
- Before a specific regimen is presented as operational in Horta/Azores, verify formulary/stock, beta-lactam allergy pathway, renal-dose references, infusion standards and microbiology turnaround; use a current antibiogram (preferably <=12 months), local and relevant to the patient, when available. No local document or stock availability is inferred from this framework review.

title: Anaphylaxis
sharedPreamble:
# Infection, allergy and respiratory modules

Shared gate: assess airway, breathing, circulation, immune status, recent healthcare
exposure, cultures, source control, allergies and prior resistant organisms. Do not
delay stabilization for diagnostic certainty.
sectionBody:
- Diagnose clinically when there is sudden compatible **airway, breathing or circulation compromise**, with or without skin/mucosal findings, after a likely trigger. Skin signs may be absent. Remove/stop the trigger if immediately feasible and call for resuscitation help.
- **Adrenaline (epinephrine) IM is first-line.** Inject into the anterolateral thigh using **1 mg/mL (1:1000)** solution. RCUK/ERC 2025 adult dose: **500 micrograms IM (0.5 mL)**. Repeat after **5 min** if airway/breathing/circulation problems persist.
- Pediatric age-banded IM doses from the RCUK full anaphylaxis guideline (2021, still the latest full guideline on the official current listing; distinct from the 2025 special-circumstances update): >12 y **500 micrograms**; 6--12 y **300 micrograms**; 6 months--6 y **150 micrograms**; <6 months **100--150 micrograms**. Use weight/local pediatric charts when available and independently double-check small-volume doses.
- Position flat with or without leg elevation unless breathing difficulty requires sitting; in pregnancy use left lateral tilt/positioning as appropriate. Give high-flow oxygen and monitoring.
- **Fluids:** give IV isotonic crystalloid early for shock and reassess. RCUK adult reference bolus **500--1000 mL**; children **10 mL/kg**, repeated according to response and overload risk.
- Progressive airway edema requires early expert airway planning. Do not delay IM adrenaline while preparing the airway.
- **Refractory anaphylaxis:** persistent airway/breathing/circulation compromise after **2 appropriate IM adrenaline doses** should trigger the refractory-anaphylaxis pathway and expert **low-dose IV adrenaline infusion** with continuous monitoring. Avoid unmonitored IV adrenaline boluses.
- Antihistamines and corticosteroids are not substitutes for IM adrenaline in life-threatening anaphylaxis. Treat bronchospasm or other persistent features as adjuncts only after adrenaline/resuscitation priorities are addressed.
- **Accepted refractory infusion reference (owner acceptance 2026-11-13):** adrenaline **1 mg made up to a final volume of 100 mL with NaCl 0.9% = 10 micrograms/mL**. Start **0.5--1 mL/kg/h**, titrating to response at the lowest effective rate under experienced critical-care supervision. Calculation: 10 micrograms/mL x 0.5--1 mL/kg/h / 60 = **0.083--0.167 micrograms/kg/min**. Continue IM adrenaline every 5 min until the infusion is running. Prime the dedicated pump line; do not piggy-back or use the arm with a BP cuff. Continuous ECG/SpO2 and frequent BP, with regular cannula/extravasation checks, are mandatory. Product-specific preparation, stability and replacement interval remain subject to verification; acceptance does not certify these details.
- **Observation/discharge (NICE NG258, 2026):** consider **2 h** observation after airway swelling has resolved and breathing, BP and HR have normalized only with a prompt response within 5--10 min to one IM dose administered within 30 min of onset, complete resolution, two in-date auto-injectors with demonstrated use and adequate adult supervision if needed. Observe at least **6 h after all symptoms resolve** if two IM doses were needed or there is previous biphasic anaphylaxis. Observe at least **12 h after all symptoms resolve** for severe reactions requiring >2 doses, severe asthma/respiratory compromise, continuing allergen absorption, out-of-hours presentation, inability to respond to deterioration or difficult emergency access. These are risk-based minima, not automatic discharge deadlines; refractory cases need critical-care assessment.
- Before discharge: provide written recurrence/emergency advice, trigger avoidance, two appropriate adrenaline auto-injectors with training when indicated and specialist allergy referral. The owner accepts this reference pathway on 2026-11-13; no named pharmacy sign-off, local stock audit or independently verified referral availability is inferred. Keep patient-specific checks and blocked automated IV contracts separate from this evidence GREEN status.

title: Toxicology
sharedPreamble:
# Renal, metabolic and toxicology modules

Shared gate: obtain glucose, ECG, electrolytes, acid-base status, renal function,
medications/toxins and volume/perfusion assessment. Repeat critical values and
verify whether results are affected by sampling error.
sectionBody:
### Entrada y seguridad
- Estabilizar **ABCDE, glucemia, temperatura, convulsiones y ECG** antes de perseguir el tóxico. Registrar agente/formulación, dosis estimada, hora, vía, coingestas, liberación prolongada, función renal/hepática, embarazo y medicación habitual. En exposición desconocida buscar toxidrome, QRS/QTc, gasometría, anion gap/osmol gap, lactato y niveles dirigidos que cambien conducta.
- El marco de reanimación toxicológica se contrasta con AHA2025 (no sólo la actualización2023); las fichas de producto y referencias del centro toxicológico delimitan dosis adultas. Contactar precozmente CIAV/centro toxicológico o toxicólogo en toxicidad grave, agente desconocido, formulación retardada, indicación de antídoto, posible depuración extracorpórea, recurrencia o intoxicación pediátrica. En parada tóxica aplicar ALS y tratar simultáneamente la causa; puede requerirse reanimación prolongada, ECTR o VA-ECMO.
- **Carbón activado no rutinario**: considerar dosis única tras ingesta potencialmente tóxica de sustancia adsorbible, sobre todo precozmente, solo con vía aérea segura. No usar por reflejo en cáusticos, hidrocarburos de alta aspiración, metales/alcoholes no adsorbibles o cuando el riesgo de aspiración supera el beneficio.
- Ninguna tabla sustituye la verificación del producto local, concentración, peso, función renal/hepática ni consulta toxicológica. Antivenenos, antitoxinas y quelantes son especialmente producto/protocolo dependientes.

### Drogas recreativas y toxidromes
- **Cocaína / crack:** no existe antídoto específico. Para agitación, hipertermia, hipertensión, taquicardia o convulsiones usar benzodiacepinas tituladas y enfriamiento activo. Tratar síndrome coronario según fisiología; si QRS ancho/arritmia por bloqueo de sodio, **bicarbonato sódico 1–2 mEq/kg IV**, repetir guiado por QRS, perfusión y gasometría. Evitar beta-bloqueo aislado no titulado en toxicidad aguda grave; seleccionar control cardiovascular con toxicología/cardiología.
- **Anfetamina, metanfetamina, MDMA, mefedrona y otras catinonas sintéticas:** sin antídoto específico. Benzodiacepinas, enfriamiento rápido en hipertermia, fluidos/electrolitos según estado, tratar hiponatremia, rabdomiólisis, convulsiones y fallo multiorgánico. No normalizar sodio rápidamente por protocolo genérico.
- **Opioides (heroína, fentanilo y análogos, metadona, oxicodona, etc.):** soporte ventilatorio primero. **Naloxona** titulada para recuperar ventilación eficaz; en dependencia conocida pueden emplearse incrementos IV pequeños (p. ej. 0.04–0.4 mg), repitiendo/escalando según respuesta; vías IN/IM son alternativas cuando no hay IV. Si recurre tras opioide de larga duración, considerar perfusión de naloxona basada en la dosis efectiva previa bajo protocolo local.
- **Benzodiacepinas / Z-drugs:** soporte. **Flumazenilo** solo en casos muy seleccionados (iatrogenia o exposición aislada en paciente no dependiente, sin proconvulsivantes/QRS ancho); referencia adulta: 0.2 mg IV lenta, repetir 0.2 mg aproximadamente cada minuto hasta respuesta, habitualmente máximo 1 mg inicial. Evitar en sobredosis mixta, dependencia, epilepsia o riesgo de abstinencia/convulsión.
- **GHB/GBL:** sin antídoto específico; vía aérea/ventilación y vigilancia. La recuperación puede ser brusca.
- **Cannabis y cannabinoides sintéticos:** sin antídoto; soporte, benzodiacepina si agitación/convulsión, evaluar isquemia, arritmia, lesión renal y coingestas en sintéticos.
- **PCP, ketamina, LSD y alucinógenos:** sin antídoto específico; ambiente controlado, benzodiacepinas para agitación/convulsiones, enfriamiento si hipertermia y tratamiento de trauma/rabdomiólisis.
- **Serotoninérgicos (ISRS/IRSN/IMAO, MDMA, tramadol, linezolid y combinaciones):** retirar agentes, benzodiacepinas, enfriamiento y soporte. En síndrome serotoninérgico moderado-grave considerar **ciproheptadina 12 mg VO/NG**, luego 2–4 mg cada 2 h hasta respuesta, con **máximo 32 mg/24 h incluyendo la carga**, según la referencia adulta CAPQ actualizada 2026. Si persiste más de 24 h, acordar continuación con toxicología. No existe formulación IV.
- **Anticolinérgicos (antihistamínicos, tricíclicos, atropínicos, plantas):** soporte, benzodiacepinas. **Fisostigmina** puede considerarse para delirium antimuscarínico puro tras ECG y consulta toxicológica; referencia adulta CAPQ: 0.5 mg IV lentamente, repetible cada 20–30 min según respuesta, **máximo 2 mg en la primera hora**, con supervisión toxicológica. Evitar con QRS ancho, sospecha de tricíclicos/bloqueo de sodio, bradicardia o trastorno de conducción.
- **Alcohol etílico:** soporte, glucosa si hipoglucemia; tiamina en riesgo de déficit antes o junto a carbohidratos cuando sea factible. No existe antídoto para la intoxicación etílica aguda.

### Analgésicos y fármacos frecuentes
- **Paracetamol/acetaminofén:** usar nomograma solo para ingesta aguda única con tiempo fiable y concentración obtenida a partir de 4 h. Iniciar **N-acetilcisteína (NAC)** si nivel en/sobre línea de tratamiento, en lesión hepática compatible o si retrasar el nivel haría iniciar >8 h tras una ingesta claramente tóxica. Usar un régimen IV/VO validado que aporte **al menos 300 mg/kg en las primeras 20–24 h**; si se usa el régimen IV clásico: 150 mg/kg en ≥1 h, 50 mg/kg en 4 h, 100 mg/kg en 16 h. No suspender por reloj: exigir criterios de parada (paracetamol bajo/indetectable, AST/ALT e INR en evolución favorable y paciente clínicamente estable).
- **Salicilatos:** no existe antídoto molecular. Alcalinizar suero/orina con bicarbonato y potasio según gasometría/electrolitos; evitar intubación si puede mantenerse ventilación espontánea. Hemodiálisis en toxicidad grave, especialmente alteración mental, hipoxemia, fracaso del tratamiento, acidosis grave o niveles altos según EXTRIP.
- **Tricíclicos y otros bloqueadores de canal de sodio (incluye difenhidramina grave, flecainida, propafenona y cocaína):** **bicarbonato sódico 1–2 mEq/kg IV** ante QRS ancho, hipotensión o arritmia ventricular, repetir guiado por respuesta y pH; evitar sobrealcalinización/hipernatremia. Lidocaína puede ser rescate especializado en arritmia ventricular persistente.
- **Bupropión:** sin antídoto; benzodiacepinas para convulsiones, soporte hemodinámico, considerar bicarbonato solo si existe bloqueo de sodio documentado (puede responder poco), ILE/ECMO en colapso refractario con toxicología.
- **Litio:** sin antídoto. Suspender, corregir volumen/electrolitos cuidadosamente y usar hemodiálisis según EXTRIP (síntomas neurológicos graves/arritmia, deterioro renal con nivel elevado o cinética de eliminación desfavorable).
- **Valproato:** soporte; considerar **L-carnitina 100 mg/kg IV (máx. 6 g) de carga, luego 15 mg/kg IV cada 4 h (máximo total 12 g/24 h)** en hiperamonemia, hepatotoxicidad, encefalopatía o intoxicación grave; considerar ECTR en toxicidad extrema según toxicología/EXTRIP.
- **Isoniazida:** convulsiones/acidosis refractarias requieren **piridoxina (vitamina B6) gramo por gramo de isoniazida ingerida**; si cantidad desconocida, referencia adulta **5 g IV en unos 10 minutos o hasta controlar convulsiones**, según referencia CAPQ, junto con benzodiacepinas y soporte; si cesan antes, acordar cómo completar la dosis con toxicología.
- **Sulfonilureas:** dextrosa para hipoglucemia + **octreótido 50 microgramos SC/IV cada 6 h**, ajustando dosis/intervalo por respuesta según toxicología en adulto para prevenir recurrencia; monitorización prolongada. En pediatría usar protocolo por peso/centro toxicológico.
- **Insulina:** no antídoto específico; dextrosa titulada (bolos + perfusión) y potasio/magnesio/fosfato seriados; evitar sobrecorrección de potasio.
- **Metformina:** no antídoto; soporte y hemodiálisis precoz en acidosis láctica grave (EXTRIP: umbral fuerte con lactato >20 mmol/L, pH ≤7.0 o fracaso de soporte; umbral menor si shock/IRA/fallo hepático).
- **Metotrexato a dosis altas con eliminación retardada/IRA:** **glucarpidasa 50 unidades/kg IV una vez durante 5 minutos** (ficha EMA) cuando cumpla criterios específicos; leucovorina debe continuar, pero no administrarla en las 2 h anteriores ni posteriores a glucarpidasa (ficha EMA). No usar glucarpidasa de forma empírica para toda sobredosis oral.
- **Colchicina:** no antídoto universalmente disponible; descontaminación precoz seleccionada, soporte intensivo y toxicología. Anticuerpos Fab específicos no son tratamiento rutinariamente disponible.
- **Digoxina y glucósidos cardiacos:** **fragmentos Fab antidigoxina** para arritmia amenazante, hiperpotasemia significativa o toxicidad grave. Dosificar por cantidad ingerida o concentración estable cuando sea posible; si no puede calcularse y existe inestabilidad vital, usar el esquema empírico del producto/centro toxicológico. No interpretar digoxinemia tras Fab con inmunoensayos convencionales como concentración libre.

### Cardiovasculares
- **Beta-bloqueadores:** soporte + vasopresores según fenotipo. **Insulina euglucémica a dosis altas**: referencia inicial 1 U/kg IV y luego 1 U/kg/h, con dextrosa para euglucemia y monitorización intensiva de glucosa/potasio; titular bajo protocolo toxicológico. **Glucagón 5–10 mg IV** puede probarse, si responde, seleccionar perfusión con toxicología: AHA2025 recoge 1–15 mg/h, ajustada al efecto; no importar la dosis de hipoglucemia; náuseas/vómitos frecuentes.
- **Calcioantagonistas:** calcio IV + **insulina euglucémica a dosis altas** precoz (1 U/kg IV, luego 1 U/kg/h y titulación), dextrosa, vasopresores; considerar ILE/ECMO en shock refractario. Calcio: usar concentración/producto local y monitorizar calcio ionizado; no intercambiar cloruro y gluconato mg por mg.
- **Clonidina/agonistas alfa-2:** soporte; naloxona puede ensayarse en casos seleccionados, especialmente pediatría, pero respuesta inconsistente.
- **Nitratos/nitritos:** si metahemoglobinemia significativa, tratar como metahemoglobinemia.
- **Antiarrítmicos clase I:** tratar bloqueo de sodio con bicarbonato; considerar lidocaína/ILE/ECMO según agente y toxicología.

### Tóxicos celulares, gases y metahemoglobina
- **Cianuro:** tratar inmediatamente si sospecha clínica grave. **Hidroxocobalamina 5 g IV** en adulto, habitualmente durante ~15 min; puede repetirse una segunda dosis de 5 g según gravedad/respuesta. Alternativa/adyuvante según toxicología: nitrito sódico + tiosulfato sódico bajo protocolo específico (Nithiodote); el nitrito puede agravar hipoxia por metahemoglobinemia, especialmente en humo/CO, anemia o reserva cardiopulmonar reducida. No administrar simultáneamente nitrito/tiosulfato por la misma vía que Cyanokit (incompatibilidad EMA). No esperar confirmación analítica.
- **Monóxido de carbono:** **100% O2**; no existe antídoto farmacológico específico. Consultar medicina hiperbárica para pérdida de conciencia, síntomas neurológicos/cardiacos, acidosis grave, embarazo con exposición significativa u otros criterios locales.
- **Metahemoglobinemia:** **azul de metileno 1–2 mg/kg IV durante 5 min**; verificar la concentración exacta: la ficha EMA de Proveblue es **5 mg/mL**, no asumir solución 1%. Una repetición se valora a 1 h según respuesta/ficha. Proveblue está **contraindicado en déficit G6PD**; evitar interacciones serotoninérgicas. La ficha limita el curso a 7 mg/kg, a 4 mg/kg en anilina/dapsona, a 2 mg/kg acumulados con eGFR 30–59 y a una dosis única 1 mg/kg con eGFR 15–29; no usar el máximo general en insuficiencia renal. Confirmar otras contraindicaciones del producto con toxicología.
- **Sulfuro de hidrógeno:** rescate seguro, O2/ventilación y soporte; no existe antídoto universal de eficacia establecida. Nitritos se han usado, pero no deben retrasar soporte y requieren toxicología.
- **Humos de incendio:** evaluar simultáneamente CO y cianuro; no asumir que una COHb baja excluye cianuro.

### Alcoholes tóxicos y solventes
- **Metanol / etilenglicol:** **fomepizol 15 mg/kg IV de carga, luego 10 mg/kg cada 12 h por 4 dosis y después 15 mg/kg cada 12 h** hasta criterios de suspensión: este esquema corresponde a la ficha estadounidense contrastada. Comprobar el producto: el SmPC de Fomepizole Waymade para etilenglicol contiene mantenimiento y ajuste en hemodiálisis diferentes; no mezclar pautas ni extrapolar a CRRT. Ajustar durante hemodiálisis según la ficha seleccionada y toxicología. Añadir folato/ácido folínico en metanol y tiamina/piridoxina en etilenglicol según protocolo. Hemodiálisis según EXTRIP por acidosis/daño de órgano/nivel/cinética.
- **Isopropanol:** no usar fomepizol de rutina; soporte. Hemodiálisis solo en casos excepcionales graves.
- **Dietilenglicol/propilenglicol:** soporte, toxicología; bloqueo de alcohol-deshidrogenasa y ECTR pueden ser considerados según agente y gravedad, sin extrapolar automáticamente el protocolo de metanol.

### Pesticidas, plantas y toxinas
- **Organofosforados/carbamatos:** descontaminación del personal/paciente, vía aérea y **atropina IV titulada rápidamente hasta secar secreciones bronquiales y mejorar ventilación/perfusión**; en adulto puede iniciarse 1–2 mg IV y duplicar cada 3–5 min si persiste síndrome muscarínico grave. **Pralidoxima** en organofosforados: referencia adulta 1–2 g IV en 15–30 min, seguida de perfusión/dosis repetidas según protocolo. Las necesidades de atropina pueden ser muy altas.
- **Rodenticidas anticoagulantes (warfarina/superwarfarinas):** vitamina K1 según INR y sangrado; las superwarfarinas pueden requerir cursos prolongados de vitamina K guiados por INR y toxicología. Hemorragia vital: seguir ruta VKA con 4F-PCC + vitamina K IV.
- **Paraquat/diquat:** no antídoto específico. Evitar hiperoxia innecesaria salvo hipoxemia; descontaminación precoz seleccionada, soporte y toxicología.
- **Estricnina:** sin antídoto; control agresivo de estímulos, benzodiacepinas y ventilación/parálisis si precisa.
- **Amanita phalloides:** soporte, NAC y silibinina IV cuando esté disponible según toxicología/hepatología; derivación precoz a centro de trasplante si insuficiencia hepática. La ficha de **Legalon SIL** (junio 2025) distingue 528,5 mg de sal de **350 mg de silibinina por vial**; no sustituir por silimarina oral. Seleccionar pauta y preparación de la ficha del producto con toxicología, sin equiparar masa de sal y principio activo.
- **Toxinas marinas (tetrodotoxina, saxitoxina, ciguatera):** predominantemente soporte; no existe antídoto específico validado para tetrodotoxina/saxitoxina. Ciguatera: tratamiento sintomático; manitol no es antídoto demostrado.
- **Mordeduras de serpiente / arañas / escorpiones:** usar **antiveneno específico del producto y especie/síndrome**, nunca una dosis genérica. Manejar coagulopatía, neurotoxicidad y shock según protocolo regional. **Viperfav** (F(ab')2 equinos) y **ViperaTAb** (Fab ovinos) tienen dosis iniciales diferentes, no intercambiables por vial o volumen. **Anascorp** es específico de Centruroides y **Antivenin Latrodectus mactans** del cuadro correspondiente; no extrapolar a cualquier escorpión/araña. Seleccionar por especie/síndrome, región y producto con toxicología, y preparar tratamiento de anafilaxia/enfermedad sérica.
- **Botulismo:** tratar precozmente la sospecha sintomática tras consulta de salud pública/toxicología. Para **BAT heptavalente equina A–G**, la ficha indica **un vial sólo como dosis de adulto desde 17 años**; niños y lactantes tienen pautas específicas del producto, nunca un vial adulto universal. **BabyBIG**, inmunoglobulina humana, corresponde al botulismo infantil A/B en menores de un año y no es intercambiable con BAT. No esperar confirmación analítica para consultar/tratar un caso compatible; vigilar hipersensibilidad durante administración.

### Metales, cáusticos y otros
- **Hierro:** **deferoxamina 15 mg/kg/h IV** en toxicidad sistémica grave, shock, acidosis o niveles indicativos; titular/duración con toxicología y vigilar hipotensión/ARDS. La referencia adulta CAPQ recoge límite de ficha 6 g/24 h; superarlo o prolongar más de 24 h requiere recomendación expresa del centro toxicológico.
- **Plomo:** quelación según nivel/síntomas. En intoxicación grave/encefalopatía seleccionar **edetato cálcico disódico (CaNa2EDTA)** solo o combinado según OMS y toxicología; dimercaprol + CaNa2EDTA es una opción, no una obligación universal. No confundir con edetato disódico sin calcio. La ficha de CaNa2EDTA contraindica anuria, enfermedad renal activa o hepatitis y advierte sobre infusión rápida en encefalopatía. **Succímero/CHEMET** oral: la ficha estadounidense es pediátrica, no indicada para encefalopatía; no atribuir autorización adulta portuguesa y vigilar hemograma/transaminasas. Dosis, vía y combinación requieren selección especializada.
- **Arsénico/mercurio:** identificar especie química, agudeza y función renal antes de seleccionar quelante con toxicología. **Dimercaprol/BAL in Oil** es IM profundo, contiene aceite de cacahuete y su ficha incluye arsénico y sales de mercurio agudas; no extrapolar a todas las formas orgánicas/crónicas. No utilizar BAL en hierro, cadmio o selenio. **DMPS/Dimaval** oral tiene indicaciones propias de mercurio y plomo crónico, diferentes de su forma inyectable y de succímero; no tratarlos como equivalentes.
- **Talio:** **azul de Prusia insoluble farmacéutico** (p. ej. Radiogardase oral) favorece eliminación gastrointestinal; no sustituir por pigmento industrial ni azul de metileno. Vigilar tránsito/estreñimiento y electrolitos; dosis/duración según producto y toxicología. Considerar ECTR en casos graves según EXTRIP.
- **Ácido fluorhídrico/fluoruros:** irrigación inmediata; **gel de gluconato cálcico 2.5%** para exposición cutánea y calcio IV/local según toxicidad, ECG y electrolitos. Las técnicas de infiltración/intraarterial requieren protocolo experto.
- **Cáusticos:** no neutralizar, no inducir vómito y no dar carbón por rutina. Evaluar vía aérea y endoscopia/imagen según lesión; manejo quirúrgico/GI temprano.
- **Hidrocarburos:** soporte respiratorio; evitar emesis/carbón rutinario por aspiración. Tratar arritmias y neumonitis según fisiología.

### Antídotos/rescates de alta prioridad — referencia rápida
| Tóxico/síndrome | Antídoto/rescate | Dosis adulta de referencia / nota |
|---|---|---|
| Opioides | Naloxona | Titular IV desde 0.04–0.4 mg en dependencia; escalar/repetir hasta ventilación eficaz; IN/IM si no IV |
| Benzodiacepina aislada seleccionada | Flumazenilo | 0.2 mg IV lenta; repetir 0.2 mg cada ~1 min; habitual máx. inicial 1 mg |
| Paracetamol | NAC | Régimen validado ≥300 mg/kg en 20–24 h; clásico IV 150 + 50 + 100 mg/kg |
| Metanol/etilenglicol | Fomepizol | 15 mg/kg carga; 10 mg/kg q12 h x4; después 15 mg/kg q12 h; ajustar en HD |
| Cianuro | Hidroxocobalamina | 5 g IV; puede repetirse 5 g |
| Metahemoglobinemia | Azul de metileno | 1–2 mg/kg IV 5 min; repetición a 1 h según ficha; concentración y límites renales verificados |
| Digoxina | Fab antidigoxina | Calcular por carga/nivel; esquema empírico solo si amenaza vital y según producto/toxicología |
| Organofosforado | Atropina | 1–2 mg IV inicial adulto, duplicar q3–5 min hasta objetivos clínicos |
| Organofosforado | Pralidoxima | 1–2 g IV en 15–30 min; después infusión/repetición según protocolo |
| Sulfonilurea | Octreótido | 50 mcg SC/IV q6 h + dextrosa; ajustar con toxicología |
| Isoniazida | Piridoxina | Gramo por gramo ingerido; si desconocido,5 g IV adulto en unos 10min o hasta control, con toxicología |
| Hierro | Deferoxamina | 15 mg/kg/h IV; límite adulto de ficha 6 g/24 h; excepciones sólo con toxicología |
| Síndrome serotoninérgico | Ciproheptadina | 12 mg VO/NG; luego2–4 mg q2 h; máx 32 mg/24 h incluida carga; consultar si >24 h |
| Anticolinérgico puro seleccionado | Fisostigmina | 0.5 mg IV lenta; repetir cada 20–30 min; máx 2 mg primera hora; ECG/contraindicaciones |
| LAST | Emulsión lipídica 20% | <70 kg: 1.5 mL/kg bolo + 0.25 mL/kg/min; máximo total 12 mL/kg |
| Beta-bloqueador/CCB | Insulina dosis alta | 1 U/kg IV + 1 U/kg/h, dextrosa y monitorización; titular por protocolo |
| Beta-bloqueador | Glucagón | 5–10 mg IV; si responde, perfusión individualizada (AHA2025: 1–15 mg/h) |
| Bloqueo de canal de sodio | Bicarbonato sódico | 1–2 mEq/kg IV, repetir guiado por QRS/pH |
| Metotrexato alta dosis + IRA | Glucarpidasa | 50 U/kg IV 5 min una vez; leucovorina separada2 h antes/después |
| Talio | Azul de Prusia | Producto farmacéutico insoluble oral; dosis según ficha/toxicología; no usar pigmento ni azul de metileno |
| HF/fluoruro | Gluconato cálcico | Gel 2.5% cutáneo; terapia IV/local según ECG, Ca/Mg/K y experto |

### Sustancias sin antídoto específico que deben estar explícitamente reconocidas
- Cocaína, anfetaminas/metanfetamina/MDMA/catinonas, GHB, cannabis/sintéticos, PCP/LSD/ketamina.
- Salicilatos (bicarbonato/diálisis son tratamientos fisiológicos, no antídoto molecular), litio, metformina, colchicina, bupropión.
- Monóxido de carbono (O2/HBO), sulfuro de hidrógeno, isopropanol, paraquat/diquat, estricnina, tetrodotoxina/saxitoxina.
- La ausencia de antídoto **no** significa ausencia de tratamiento: definir soporte, descontaminación selectiva, ECTR/ECMO y criterios de escalada.

### Reversión de anticoagulantes e hipocoagulantes
- Ruta detallada en `anticoagulation-reversal`. Toxicología debe reconocer: VKA/warfarina y superwarfarinas; heparina no fraccionada; HBPM; fondaparinux; dabigatrán; apixabán/rivaroxabán/edoxabán; argatrobán/bivalirudina; y anticoagulantes de uso infrecuente. Diferenciar antídoto específico, reversión parcial e inespecífica.
- **Disponibilidad local:** el propietario confirma el 13/11/2026: «tenemos todos los antidotos a disposicion». Se cierra ese pendiente como declaración del servicio; no se infieren marcas, lotes ni firma farmacéutica independiente. En cada uso, verificar el producto real, concentración, preparación, contraindicaciones y condiciones de administración. La capacidad de hemodiálisis/ECMO se decide por circuito específico y no se deduce de disponer de antídotos.
- **Contraste de productos infrecuentes completado en el alcance almacenado:** ver `qa/TOXICOLOGY_RARE_PRODUCTS_REVIEW_2026-11-13.md` y su matriz de 17 referencias. Las fichas extranjeras identifican límites de producto; no certifican autorización/comercialización portuguesa de cada marca.

title: Pediatric Emergencies
sharedPreamble:
# Special-population modules

Shared gate: adjust thresholds, communication, consent, safeguarding, doses and
disposition to physiology, developmental stage, pregnancy and baseline function.
sectionBody:
- Use pediatric assessment triangle/ABCDE, age-specific vitals and weight in kilograms; use measured weight or a validated estimate when necessary.
- Calculate every high-risk drug and fluid dose with units, maximum cap, concentration and independent check. Use current pediatric resuscitation guidance.
- Consider safeguarding and family communication. Lower the threshold for pediatric critical-care input when trajectory, age or resources increase risk.

title: Pediatric Procedural Sedation
sharedPreamble:
# Special-population modules

Shared gate: adjust thresholds, communication, consent, safeguarding, doses and
disposition to physiology, developmental stage, pregnancy and baseline function.
sectionBody:
- Scope: procedural sedation/analgesia in children in ED/acute care. This is **not** RSI and not continuous PICU sedation. Define the procedure goal: anxiolysis, analgesia, immobility, amnesia or dissociation; use non-pharmacologic support and local/regional anaesthesia whenever appropriate.
- **Safety prerequisites:** trained pediatric sedation clinician, airway-skilled staff, resuscitation equipment immediately available, baseline HR/RR/BP/SpO2, continuous observation of airway/chest movement, pulse oximetry and cardiorespiratory monitoring appropriate to depth/agent. Combined opioids + sedatives increase respiratory risk.
- **Ketamine IV:** RCH procedural sedation guidance: initial **1--1.5 mg/kg IV over 1--2 min** immediately before the procedure; additional **0.25--0.5 mg/kg IV every 10 min** if required. Maximum cumulative **4.5 mg/kg**, but doses >2.5 mg/kg are associated with more adverse events and should trigger reconsideration of the strategy.
- **Ketamine IM:** initial **4 mg/kg IM**; a repeat **2 mg/kg IM after 10 min** may be given if sedation is inadequate. RCH lists a maximum cumulative reference of **6 mg/kg**. Ketamine procedural sedation is absolutely contraindicated in infants **<3 months** in this guideline and requires senior review in infants <12 months and in higher-risk airway/respiratory/cardiac situations.
- **Ketamine monitoring/recovery:** expect dissociation, nystagmus and mild HR/BP rise. Be prepared for vomiting, transient laryngospasm and rare apnea/respiratory depression. Do not discharge until the child has returned to premorbid neurologic baseline and can mobilize/verbalize at baseline level as developmentally appropriate.
- **Nitrous oxide/oxygen:** useful for short painful/distressing procedures; RCH supports continuous-flow mixtures titratable **30--70% nitrous oxide**, and states it is safe to start at **70%** when appropriately monitored. A 50:50 premixed nitrous/oxygen system may be used on demand. Procedures >30 min have more vomiting/side effects.
- **Intranasal fentanyl:** for children **>=12 months** with moderate/severe pain and no IV access, RCH: first dose **1.5 micrograms/kg IN**; repeat **0.75--1.5 micrograms/kg after 5--10 min** if needed. RCH caps the first dose at **100 micrograms** with the 300 micrograms/mL solution (usual maximum **75 micrograms** with 50 micrograms/mL); repeat-dose maximum is **75--100 micrograms** according to product. Use ideal body weight in overweight children; reassess after two doses rather than continuing an open-ended sequence. Product/concentration matters: RCH currently describes **300 micrograms/mL** hospital nasal solution for lower-volume delivery; do not automatically use an older 50 micrograms/mL IV presentation intranasally without verifying the product.
- **Opioid rescue:** excessive sedation/respiratory depression requires airway support and naloxone according to the pediatric opioid-toxicity pathway. Do not rely on naloxone in place of ventilation.
- **Agent selection:** ketamine is appropriate for short painful procedures needing immobilisation (for example fracture reduction, laceration repair, abscess drainage, foreign-body removal). Nitrous oxide is suited to short procedures with modest analgesic needs. Midazolam provides anxiolysis/amnesia but limited analgesia; do not substitute it for analgesia in a painful procedure.
- **Fasting:** urgency and aspiration risk should be considered, but time-critical procedures must not be delayed solely to meet an arbitrary fasting interval. Follow current pediatric sedation/anaesthesia guidance and document risk-benefit.
- **Failure/escalation:** if target sedation cannot be achieved safely within the source dose envelope, stop stacking doses and reassess the plan; involve anaesthesia for deeper sedation/general anaesthesia when required.
- **Monitoring/recovery reconciliation (AAP/AAPD reaffirmed June 2025):** designate a trained observer and staff capable of rescue from deeper-than-intended sedation. Use continuous oxygenation and ventilation monitoring; capnography is required for deep sedation, with documented exceptions when not feasible. Record time-stamped vital signs and all doses through recovery. Continue observation after naloxone/flumazenil because re-sedation can outlast the antagonist. Discharge only at baseline with a responsible adult and written instructions. This reference does not certify local staffing/equipment or authorize unrestricted sedative combinations.
- **Nitrous-specific safety:** exclude airway compromise and trapped-gas conditions (for example pneumothorax/bowel obstruction), and do not use with GCS<15 after head injury. Give100% oxygen for3--5min after stopping and monitor saturation during recovery. Higher nitrous concentrations or combinations with other sedatives require the appropriate deeper-sedation monitoring/rescue capability.

title: Pediatric Acute Respiratory Support
sharedPreamble:
# Special-population modules

Shared gate: adjust thresholds, communication, consent, safeguarding, doses and
disposition to physiology, developmental stage, pregnancy and baseline function.
sectionBody:
- Scope: acute oxygenation/ventilation support in infants and children beyond neonatal transition. Combine with the cause-specific pathway (bronchiolitis, asthma, pneumonia, sepsis, neuromuscular disease, cardiac disease, intoxication, etc.). No single respiratory rate, SpO2 or blood-gas value substitutes for trajectory and work of breathing.
- **Initial oxygen:** ERC/RCUK 2025: in respiratory, circulatory or neurological failure, start **100% oxygen** initially, then titrate FiO2 as soon as reliable SpO2 is available. In previously healthy children target **SpO2 94--98%**, using the lowest FiO2 that achieves at least about 94%. Individualise targets in cyanotic congenital heart disease or chronic respiratory failure.
- **Conventional oxygen failure:** consider humidified high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO/HFNC) or CPAP/NIV when hypoxaemia does not respond adequately to conventional oxygen and the child retains sufficient respiratory drive. Do not allow non-invasive support to delay intubation in exhaustion, deteriorating consciousness, refractory hypoxaemia, shock or inability to protect the airway.
- **HFNO flow by weight (RCH):** for **<=12 kg use 2 L/kg/min**. For **>12 kg**, use **2 L/kg/min for the first 12 kg + 0.5 L/kg/min for each kg above 12 kg**, maximum **50 L/min**. Increase to prescribed flow over a few minutes/as tolerated.
- **HFNO oxygen:** RCH starts high-flow system flow in room air (21%) and then adds oxygen according to saturation/clinical need. Do not assume high flow automatically means high FiO2.
- **HFNO response gate:** if there is no clinical stabilisation within **2 h**, obtain PICU/critical-care review; if not stabilising within **4 h**, consider PICU transfer/escalation. Reassess respiratory rate/effort, HR, SpO2/FiO2, mental state, perfusion and gas exchange.
- **CPAP/NIV:** use only where the child can be closely monitored and rapidly escalated. RCH states acute respiratory failure requiring CPAP/NIV should be managed in a PICU-capable pathway; initiation may occur in ED/PICU. Contraindications include respiratory arrest, unstable cardiorespiratory status, inability to protect the airway, uncooperative patient where interface cannot be safely used, and relevant facial/oral/oesophageal surgery/injury.
- **Do not import adult NIV settings:** pediatric CPAP/IPAP/EPAP are disease-, age-, interface- and device-specific. This module deliberately does not copy the adult IPAP 10--15 / EPAP 4 starting rule. Use a pediatric respiratory/PICU protocol and titrate to work of breathing, ventilation, oxygenation and comfort.
- **Bag-mask ventilation:** ERC/RCUK 2025 recommends BMV as first-line support for inadequate spontaneous ventilation. Use correct head position, mask size/seal and a two-person technique when difficult; provide enough pressure/time for visible but not excessive chest rise and avoid hyperinflation.
- **Ventilation rate reference during supported ventilation:** ERC/RCUK 2025 pragmatic rates are about **25/min in infants**, **20/min in children >1 y**, **15/min in children >8 y**, and **10/min in children >12 y**, adjusted to physiology and gas exchange.
- **Invasive ventilation after intubation:** in previously healthy children start around **6--8 mL/kg ideal body weight** tidal volume and **PEEP 5 cm H2O**, then individualise PEEP/FiO2 and respiratory rate to oxygenation/ventilation targets. Use continuous ETCO2, confirm PaCO2 relationship with blood gas and avoid both hypo- and hyperventilation.
- **Sudden deterioration on support:** use DOPES: displacement, obstruction, pneumothorax/pathology, equipment, stomach/stacking/sedation. Revert to bag-mask ventilation and troubleshoot immediately when device failure or airway problem is suspected.
- **Escalation triggers:** rising oxygen requirement, persistent severe retractions/grunting, apnea, fatigue, reduced respiratory drive, worsening hypercapnia/acidosis, haemodynamic instability or deteriorating mental state -> senior/PICU review and invasive airway planning.
- **Reassessment overrides clock thresholds:** deterioration requires immediate escalation; the HFNO 2 h review / 4 h transfer checkpoints are not permission to wait. Nasal prongs must not occlude the nares. The RCH room-air initiation is a device/flow setup approach, not a reason to remove needed oxygen from a severely hypoxaemic child. Pediatric CPAP/NIV settings require an explicit disease/device protocol and a ready invasive-airway rescue plan.

title: Pediatric Cns Infection
sharedPreamble:
# Special-population modules

Shared gate: adjust thresholds, communication, consent, safeguarding, doses and
disposition to physiology, developmental stage, pregnancy and baseline function.
sectionBody:
- Scope: suspected bacterial meningitis or encephalitis in children beyond the neonatal pathway. Obtain blood cultures and perform lumbar puncture before antimicrobials only when safe and when this does not materially delay treatment.
- Timing: RCH advises antibiotics within **30 min of the decision to treat**; NICE NG240 requires IV antibiotics **within 1 h of hospital arrival**. If LP is contraindicated or delayed >30 min, treat first. A normal CT does not exclude raised ICP.
- Age >=2 months: ceftriaxone **100 mg/kg IV every 24 h, max 4 g**, or cefotaxime **50 mg/kg IV every 6 h, max 2 g**. If pneumococcal resistance is a concern or Gram-positive cocci are seen, add vancomycin using age/renal-function-specific dosing and therapeutic monitoring. The RCH **15 mg/kg IV every 6 h, max 750 mg per dose** starting reference applies to children **>90 days with normal renal function**; infants <=90 days require the infant-specific regimen and pharmacy/specialist input, not automatic q6h dosing.
- Age 1--2 months: use a young-infant regimen. RCH lists benzylpenicillin **60 mg/kg IV every 4 h** once >4 weeks plus cefotaxime **50 mg/kg IV every 6 h**; ceftriaxone **100 mg/kg IV every 24 h, max 2 g in this 0--2-month RCH table** may be used after 4 weeks only when product/age restrictions permit. Avoid ceftriaxone in premature infants <41 weeks corrected gestation and in neonates receiving calcium-containing IV solutions.
- Meningococcal disease: give a third-generation cephalosporin immediately; RCH uses ceftriaxone **100 mg/kg IV daily, max 4 g** when >4 weeks. Do not delay for investigations in an unstable child.
- Adjunct dexamethasone: for children >=2 months with presumed bacterial meningitis, RCH uses **0.15 mg/kg IV every 6 h, max 10 mg**, started just before or with the first antibiotic dose. The selected RCH reference duration is **4 days**; review continuation against the identified organism and specialist advice. Other guideline durations must remain explicitly attributed.
- Possible HSV encephalitis: add aciclovir promptly. RCH: <3 months corrected age **20 mg/kg IV every 8 h** (>30 weeks gestation); age 3 months--12 years **500 mg/m2 IV every 8 h** or **20 mg/kg IV every 8 h**; >12 years **10 mg/kg IV every 8 h**. Adjust for renal function and ensure hydration.
- Manage shock, seizures, sodium/glucose abnormalities and raised-ICP physiology in parallel. Use droplet precautions when meningococcal/Hib disease is suspected until the applicable isolation period is complete.
- Reassess antimicrobials when CSF/PCR/cultures identify the organism. Typical pathogen-specific durations differ; do not use one universal duration.
- **Procedure/diagnosis safety:** shock, uncontrolled seizures, significant depressed consciousness or raised-ICP signs preclude an immediate LP; stabilize and treat first. Suspected HSV requires renal-adjusted IV aciclovir and hydration while diagnostic work proceeds. A general sepsis ceftriaxone dose is not the meningitis dose. Neonatal contraindications in the dispensed product still apply even when another guideline permits ceftriaxone.

title: Pediatric Dka
sharedPreamble:
# Special-population modules

Shared gate: adjust thresholds, communication, consent, safeguarding, doses and
disposition to physiology, developmental stage, pregnancy and baseline function.
sectionBody:
- Scope: diabetic ketoacidosis in children/adolescents. Do not use the adult DKA/HHS fluid/bicarbonate pathway. Diagnostic triad: glucose >11 mmol/L, venous pH <7.3 or bicarbonate <18 mmol/L, and ketonaemia >=3 mmol/L or urine ketones >=2+.
- Start ABC monitoring, neurological observations, cardiac monitoring when potassium is abnormal, measured weight and frequent bedside glucose/electrolyte/ketone checks. Cerebral injury is the key life-threatening complication.
- Fluids: RCH 2025 starts with 0.9% sodium chloride. In a tachycardic child with delayed central capillary refill, give **10 mL/kg 0.9% sodium chloride over 30 min** and reassess. Rare shock requires cause-directed resuscitation and senior/PICU input; avoid reflex repeated rapid boluses.
- Potassium: use **40 mmol/L KCl** in rehydration fluid when serum K <=5.5 mmol/L and urine output is established; may increase to **60 mmol/L** if required. If K <3.0 mmol/L, replace potassium before insulin. Do not add potassium to a bag already hanging.
- Begin IV insulin only after **1 h of IV rehydration**. Do **not** give an insulin bolus. RCH: **0.1 units/kg/h** for most children; consider **0.05 units/kg/h** for age <5 y, inter-hospital transfer/limited biochemical monitoring, or BGL <15 mmol/L when insulin starts.
- Source-supported pump preparations: **1 unit/mL** (50 units in final 50 mL) or **0.1 unit/mL** (50 units in final 500 mL). The calculator reports mL/h for both concentrations; use one clearly labelled concentration and avoid decimal/concentration switching.
- Glucose: when BGL <=15 mmol/L, change to 0.9% sodium chloride with **5% glucose** plus potassium as indicated. If glucose falls <5 mmol/L or is dropping >5 mmol/L/h while acidosis persists, increase glucose to **10%** before reducing insulin. Aim BGL about 5--10 mmol/L while ketosis/acidosis resolves.
- Hypoglycaemia <4 mmol/L: give **10% glucose 2 mL/kg IV**, repeat if needed, and continue insulin while increasing glucose delivery. If glucose continues to fall despite 10% glucose, step insulin down (for example 0.1 -> 0.05 units/kg/h) under the pediatric DKA pathway.
- Corrected sodium (RCH): **corrected Na = measured Na + 0.4 x (glucose - 5.5)** with glucose in mmol/L. Track direction of corrected sodium and osmolality; discuss corrected Na <125 or >150 mmol/L early.
- Cerebral injury: do not wait for imaging. Elevate head, reduce fluid rate by about one-third and give either **mannitol 20% 0.5 g/kg IV over 20 min** or **3% sodium chloride 3 mL/kg IV over 15 min**; if no response within 15 min, escalate urgently to PICU/critical care.
- Bicarbonate is not routine. RCH restricts it to exceptional situations such as life-threatening hyperkalaemia or severe circulatory failure requiring inotropes, with intensive-care input.
- Transition to subcutaneous insulin only when alert, eating and metabolically stable (pH >7.3, bicarbonate >18 mmol/L); overlap rapid-acting subcutaneous insulin with the IV infusion for **30--60 min**.
- Use pediatric_dka_calculator.py for corrected sodium, insulin pump rates and emergency cerebral-injury doses. These arithmetic outputs do not replace serial biochemical/neurological reassessment.
- **Monitoring and transition boundary:** measure potassium within 1 h of starting insulin and subsequently at 2--4 h intervals as clinically indicated; continue frequent glucose/neurologic checks. The **30--60 min overlap is for the first rapid-acting SC dose** in the RCH transition. It is not a basal-only conversion rule; coordinate basal coverage and the meal/SC regimen with pediatric endocrinology. Never import the adult insulin-bolus or IV-to-basal schedule into this pathway. Ensure early PICU/retrieval discussion for coma, shock, seizures, cerebral-injury signs or severe acidosis.

title: Pediatric Sepsis
sharedPreamble:
# Special-population modules

Shared gate: adjust thresholds, communication, consent, safeguarding, doses and
disposition to physiology, developmental stage, pregnancy and baseline function.
sectionBody:
- Scope: suspected sepsis/septic shock in infants, children and adolescents outside the immediate neonatal-transition pathway. Use age-specific recognition and the source-specific infection pathway in parallel.
- Timing: SSC 2026 recommends antimicrobials for suspected septic shock **as soon as possible, ideally within 1 h**. For probable sepsis without shock, perform a rapid time-limited evaluation and, if concern persists, start antimicrobials **ideally within 3 h**. NICE NG254 requires broad-spectrum antimicrobials **within 1 h** once a child meets high-risk criteria.
- Community-acquired sepsis, age >=28 days and <16 years: NICE uses ceftriaxone **80 mg/kg IV once daily, max 4 g**. In infants <3 months add Listeria-active coverage (for example ampicillin/amoxicillin). Use the pediatric antibiotic registry rather than an adult sepsis regimen.
- Newborn <28 days with community-acquired sepsis: NICE permits ceftriaxone **50 mg/kg once daily** only when corrected gestational age is >40 weeks and the infant is not receiving IV calcium; otherwise use cefotaxime **50 mg/kg every 6--12 h** according to age. Early-onset neonatal sepsis remains a neonatal pathway.
- Fluids (SSC 2026, ICU-capable setting): use **10--20 mL/kg per bolus**, reassessing after each bolus, up to **40--60 mL/kg in the first hour** if shock persists and there are no signs of overload. Prefer balanced/buffered crystalloid when appropriate; 0.9% saline is acceptable and may be preferred in selected sodium/CNS situations.
- Stop fluid escalation when shock resolves or signs of overload develop. Use capillary refill, pulse quality, mental state, urine output, blood pressure, extremity temperature, lactate trend and POCUS when available to refine phenotype.
- Vasoactives: do not delay for central access; SSC 2026 supports peripheral initiation when needed. There is **insufficient evidence to prefer epinephrine over norepinephrine or vice versa universally** as first-line pediatric septic-shock therapy. Choose by hemodynamic phenotype and titrate to perfusion.
- If high-dose catecholamines are required, SSC 2026 suggests either adding vasopressin or further titrating catecholamines. Inodilator use for myocardial dysfunction remains individualized because evidence is insufficient for a universal recommendation.
- Corticosteroids: do **not** routinely give hydrocortisone when hemodynamic stability is restored with fluids/vasoactives. If shock remains unstable despite adequate resuscitation and vasoactives, evidence is insufficient for a universal hydrocortisone recommendation; however, give stress-dose hydrocortisone when adrenal insufficiency is suspected or documented.
- Oxygen-guideline boundary: SSC 2026 suggests a conservative SpO2 range after resuscitation, while ERC/RCUK pediatric respiratory guidance generally targets 94--98% in previously healthy children with acute failure. Do not silently merge these targets; route active respiratory failure to pediatric-acute-respiratory-support and individualize.
- Obtain cultures before antibiotics when this can be done rapidly without delaying treatment. Identify and control drainable/removable sources promptly, and de-escalate antimicrobials when microbiology and clinical trajectory permit.
- **Resource boundary (SSC 2026):** without intensive-care availability, do not give bolus fluid for sepsis without hypotension; with hypotensive septic shock, the suggested first-hour ceiling is **40 mL/kg**, with reassessment after every bolus. Do not require an arbitrary cumulative volume before starting a needed vasoactive. The post-resuscitation SSC **SpO2 88--92%** suggestion is conditional and is not the initial target for an actively failing airway/respiratory resuscitation. For confirmed source/resistant-organism risk use the relevant empiric pathway; urgent initial antibiotics can change with local resistance risk as well as subsequent cultures.
- **Neonatal product boundary:** the NICE >40-week criterion above does not overrule stricter prematurity, hyperbilirubinaemia or calcium restrictions in the dispensed ceftriaxone label; choose the neonatal alternative when contraindicated.
- **Portugal comparison:** DGS014/2018 (PAI fever,03/08/2018, hospital risk pathway) describes a20mL/kg saline bolus and immediate third-generation cephalosporin100mg/kg/dose, plus ampicillin in infants<3months. This differs from the NICE80mg/kg/day general-sepsis reference above and must not be silently substituted, averaged or repeated as an open-ended100mg/kg schedule. The updated international reference uses SSC2026 reassessment/resource limits and explicitly attributed antibiotic regimens; apply the service-approved age/source regimen. The official index still lists DGS014/2018 without a revocation marker in the retrieved entry; this review does not certify exhaustive national supersession or local adoption.

title: Pediatric Hematology Oncology Emergencies
sharedPreamble:
# Special-population modules

Shared gate: adjust thresholds, communication, consent, safeguarding, doses and
disposition to physiology, developmental stage, pregnancy and baseline function.
sectionBody:
- Scope: oncology/hematology emergencies in children, particularly febrile neutropenia, hyperleukocytosis/leukostasis, tumour lysis syndrome (TLS), sickle-cell acute chest/fever/stroke, severe anemia/thrombocytopenia and treatment complications. Contact the treating hematology/oncology team early, but **do not delay the first time-critical treatment while waiting for contact**.
- **Febrile neutropenia is a medical emergency.** RCH defines fever as a single temperature >=38.5 °C or >=38.0 °C sustained for 1 h, and neutropenia as ANC <500/mm3 or <1000/mm3 with predicted fall to <500/mm3 within 48 h.
- Give the first IV antibiotic **within 30 min when sepsis/systemic compromise is present** and **within 60 min otherwise**. Obtain blood cultures (including CVAD lumens where applicable) before antibiotics only if this does not delay treatment.
- RCH clinically stable first-line: piperacillin-tazobactam **100 mg/kg IV every 6 h, max 4 g/dose** (dose refers to piperacillin component). Non-life-threatening penicillin allergy: cefepime **50 mg/kg IV q8h, max 2 g** preferred, or ceftazidime **50 mg/kg IV q8h, max 2 g**.
- Immediate/life-threatening beta-lactam allergy: RCH uses ciprofloxacin **10 mg/kg IV q12h, max 400 mg** plus vancomycin **15 mg/kg IV q6h, max 500 mg**, with therapeutic drug monitoring. Local resistance/allergy expertise still applies.
- Systemic compromise/sepsis, high-risk cancer treatment or inpatient-onset FN: add amikacin **22.5 mg/kg IV q24h** (or **18 mg/kg if >10 y**), max **1.5 g**, with drug-level/renal monitoring. Do not co-infuse aminoglycosides through the same unflushed line as piperacillin-type penicillins.
- Suspected resistant Gram-positive infection (infected CVAD, cellulitis, proven Gram-positive bacteraemia, relevant MRSA colonisation) may require vancomycin; **persistent fever alone in a clinically stable child is not an indication to add vancomycin**. Abdominal/perineal infection may require anaerobic coverage when the base regimen lacks it.
- In febrile neutropenic sepsis, RCH uses an initial **0.9% saline 20 mL/kg IV over <=10 min**, reassessing after each bolus; additional boluses may be used to a cumulative **40 mL/kg**, with senior review before larger volumes and early vasoactive support if perfusion does not improve. Reconcile this older oncology-specific fluid approach with `pediatric-sepsis`/SSC 2026 rather than automatically giving 40 mL/kg.
- **Hyperleukocytosis:** WCC >100 x10^9/L is high-count leukaemia; AML can develop leukostasis at lower counts (around >=50 x10^9/L). Neurological or respiratory dysfunction may represent leukostasis and requires urgent oncology/PICU/retrieval involvement.
- Hyperleukocytosis supportive care (RCH 2025): hyperhydrate at **125 mL/m2/h or about double maintenance** using **0.9% sodium chloride + 5% glucose without added potassium**; monitor FBE/electrolytes/calcium-magnesium-phosphate/uric acid frequently. Maintain platelets **>50 x10^9/L**, correct coagulopathy and avoid routine red-cell transfusion because increasing viscosity can worsen leukostasis.
- If red cells are essential in hyperleukocytosis, discuss with oncology and use small aliquots; RCH limits transfusion to about **5--10 mL/kg** to reduce hyperviscosity risk. Rasburicase/allopurinol and cytoreduction are oncology-directed; check G6PD status before rasburicase because of haemolysis/methemoglobinaemia risk.
- **Tumour lysis syndrome:** anticipate before chemotherapy in bulky/high-count disease. Monitor potassium, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, creatinine and ECG; avoid adding potassium to hyperhydration. Treat life-threatening hyperkalaemia/hypocalcaemic arrhythmia using the pediatric electrolyte pathway and involve nephrology/PICU early for refractory electrolyte disturbance or renal failure.
- **Sickle-cell disease:** fever is high-risk because of functional asplenia; obtain cultures and give prompt IV third-generation cephalosporin per the sickle-cell/ID pathway. Chest pain, hypoxaemia or respiratory symptoms should be treated as possible **acute chest syndrome**, not as uncomplicated vaso-occlusive pain.
- Acute chest syndrome: oxygen (RCH target >96% in its sickle-cell pathway), early antibiotics including a third-generation cephalosporin plus atypical coverage, analgesia, cautious hydration and early PICU/hematology input. Avoid fluid overload because it can worsen pulmonary disease.
- Sickle vaso-occlusive pain: give analgesia promptly; RCH includes morphine **0.05 mg/kg IV per dose** for moderate-severe pain, repeated/titrated using the pediatric pain pathway. Hydration should restore euvolaemia, not produce indiscriminate overhydration.
- Sickle stroke/acute neurological deficit: urgent neuroimaging and hematology/neurology input; transfusion support and red-cell exchange may be required. Do not delay specialist transfer while treating ABC abnormalities.
- **Transfusion boundary:** blood-component thresholds in oncology/sickle-cell disease differ from major haemorrhage. Route component dosing to `pediatric-blood-transfusion-major-hemorrhage` only when hemorrhage physiology is present; otherwise follow disease-specific hematology guidance.
- **2026 sepsis reconciliation:** for active resuscitation follow `pediatric-sepsis`/SSC2026 with10--20mL/kg aliquots and reassessment; stop for overload and escalate vasoactives/transfer when indicated. The older RCH oncology20mL/kg/40mL/kg text above remains an attributed comparator, not a mandatory bolus sequence. Oncology hyperhydration is not a shock bolus and must be individualized for renal/cardiac dysfunction or fluid overload.
- **Disease-specific medication boundary:** the RCH febrile-neutropenia vancomycin maximum500mg differs from the general RCH pediatric monograph; preserve the attributed oncology regimen and use age/renal-specific specialist/TDM review, especially in young infants. Rasburicase is contraindicated with G6PD deficiency; do not treat unknown G6PD status as a negative test. Suspected TLS requires urgent specialist assessment; asymptomatic hypocalcaemia is not an automatic calcium-replacement indication. Persistent fever alone does not justify indiscriminate antibiotic escalation.

title: Pediatric Drowning Hypothermia
sharedPreamble:
# Special-population modules

Shared gate: adjust thresholds, communication, consent, safeguarding, doses and
disposition to physiology, developmental stage, pregnancy and baseline function.
sectionBody:
- Scope: drowning/submersion injury and accidental hypothermia in infants, children and adolescents. Drowning is defined by respiratory impairment from submersion/immersion; avoid obsolete labels such as 'near-drowning' or 'secondary drowning'.
- **Immediate priority is oxygenation/ventilation.** ERC 2025 emphasizes reversing hypoxia before cardiac arrest. Remove the child from water as rapidly and safely as possible; trained rescuers may provide ventilation in water when safe. Once on a safe surface, start pediatric BLS with **5 rescue breaths** before standard CPR when the child is not breathing.
- Give **100% oxygen** as soon as available and titrate after stabilization. Intubate/ventilate when there is persistent respiratory failure, inadequate respiratory drive or inability to protect the airway. Treat pulmonary oedema/ARDS supportively; prophylactic antibiotics are **not routinely indicated** unless there is infection/sepsis or grossly contaminated-water exposure.
- Evaluate why the drowning occurred: seizure, arrhythmia/long-QT, hypoglycaemia, intoxication, trauma, supervision/safeguarding issue or deliberate self-harm in an adolescent. Cervical-spine injury is uncommon unless a traumatic mechanism such as diving is present.
- **Hypothermia with circulation:** remove wet clothes, dry and insulate, handle gently and monitor core temperature with a low-reading thermometer when available. ERC 2025 recommends active rewarming when core temperature is **<35 °C**, aiming for at least **1 °C/h** and stopping active rewarming around **35 °C** to avoid overshoot.
- Apply active external warming mainly to the **trunk** (chest, abdomen, back, axillae), not by aggressively heating/rubbing extremities. Avoid hot-water immersion or a warm shower in a child with reduced consciousness because of vasodilation/after-drop risk.
- Give warmed humidified oxygen and warmed IV/IO fluids at about **39--42 °C** when fluids are clinically required, while avoiding fluid overload. ERC indicates active internal rewarming for severe hypothermia, especially **<30 °C**, and early expert/ECLS-centre discussion for severe instability or arrest.
- **Hypothermic cardiac arrest:** start CPR; do not use a minimum core temperature as a reason to withhold resuscitation. Prolonged resuscitation may have good neurological outcome in selected severely hypothermic children.
- When core temperature is **<30 °C**, ERC 2025 advises a maximum of **3 defibrillation attempts** for a shockable rhythm until the temperature rises above 30 °C. Give only a single adrenaline dose below 30 °C unless immediate ECLS is planned, and **do not give amiodarone until temperature >30 °C**.
- Between **30 and 35 °C**, prolong resuscitation-drug intervals: ERC uses adrenaline approximately **every 8 min** and delays the next amiodarone dose similarly. Above 35 °C return to the standard pediatric ALS drug/defibrillation sequence.
- Transport hypothermic arrest without ROSC, or severe hypothermia with imminent-arrest features (markedly reduced consciousness, ventricular arrhythmia or hypotension), to an extracorporeal life-support capable centre whenever feasible.
- **Observation after drowning:** an alert/asymptomatic child does not need routine investigations. Chest X-ray findings correlate poorly with outcome. RCH discharge criteria include observation for **8 h from the drowning event**, remaining asymptomatic with normal respiratory examination and **SpO2 >=95%** on room air, plus no unresolved medical/safety concern.
